title: Add compact-span rollups and tenant-priority alert ranker with trace thumbnails
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: We continue to see noisy long-tail alerts driven by sparse but heavy-cost traces across tenants. Root cause is twofold: high-cardinality span detail retained per-invocation and flat alert scoring that treats all span-origin signals equally. This PR introduces (1) a compact-span rollup format to reduce telemetry cardinality while preserving phase/timing fidelity and cost attribution and (2) a tenant-priority alert ranker that orders SLO alerts by a tunable mix of customer SLA tier, recent cost drift, and invocation impact.

What this PR does: Adds a compact-span encoder/rollup pipeline, a lightweight trace-thumbnail generator for the UI, a pluggable alert-ranking service, and a dashboard widget to visualize ranker inputs and outcomes. Implements a conservative rollout plan with a default opt-in for safety-critical tenants.

Technical summary: compact-span rollups aggregate contiguous low-information spans into single summarized entries while preserving timing boundaries, KV cache hit/miss flags, and per-token cost slices. The rollup encoder runs as a post-processor in the telemetry pipeline and outputs a new metric family (telemetry.compact_span.rollup.v1) plus a compressed proto for trace-thumbnails. The alert ranker ingests annotated SLO signals and enriches alerts with rank_score = weighted_sum(SLA_weight, cost_delta_zscore, long_tail_score, recent_false_positive_penalty). Rank weights are configurable via the observability-config API and default to conservative values.

Files changed (high level): services/telemetry/rollup/compact_span_encoder.py, services/telemetry/rollup/tests/test_compact_encoder.py, metrics/migrations/001_add_compact_span_metrics.sql, observability/alerting/ranker.py, observability/alerting/config/defaults.yaml, webapp/console/src/components/TraceThumbnail.tsx, webapp/console/src/pages/observability/RankerDebugPanel.tsx, dashboards/observability/compact-span-ranker.json5, ci/telemetry_integration.yml, docs/observability/compact-span-rollups.md

Rollout plan and safety: Default behavior is off for existing tenants; new telemetry consumers are given opt-in via the console and API. We add a canary: enabled for 3 internal tenants and test traffic for 72 hours, then enable a tiered expansion (5%, 25%, 100%) with manual gates and automated anomaly checks. Alert ranker defaults to score-neutral mode (rank-only, no suppression) for the first week, then will be allowed to suppress lower-ranked noisy alerts behind a feature flag.

Testing: Unit tests added for encoder edge cases (overlapping spans, late-arriving events, large KV blobs). Integration test simulates high-cardinality invocation streams and verifies rollup size reduction and stable token-cost attribution within 2% error. End-to-end visual tests for TraceThumbnail component and RankerDebugPanel. CI required a flaky test rerun (telemetry_integration.test_large_stream) which passed after increasing mock timeouts.

Migration notes: Adds a backward-compatible metric namespace (telemetry.compact_span.rollup.v1). Old consumers continue to receive full spans until they subscribe to rollups; migration docs include recommended mapping rules and a small script for converting historical sampled spans to rollups for dashboard backfills.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Dashboard and UI component added - [x] Migration docs written - [x] Rollout plan documented in docs/observability/compact-span-rollups.md

Related: ENG-913 for alert prioritization work; ENG-1023 telemetry cardinality initiative.

release_notes: Introduces compact-span rollups (telemetry.compact_span.rollup.v1), a tenant-priority alert ranker, and a TraceThumbnail UI component. Rollout is opt-in with canary phase. See docs/observability/compact-span-rollups.md for migration and configuration details.
additional_notes: This PR intentionally keeps the rollup binary small (LZ4 compressed proto) to reduce storage and query costs. We will monitor query patterns for two weeks and iterate on ranker weights based on SRE feedback.
